transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I’m having trouble keeping my mind on the work I’m supposed to be doing. In the lab, even on grant calls or safety meetings, something small will catch me—a pump vibration, a student saying something off to the side, an odd peak in an old spectrum—and then I’m off chasing that for hours. Meanwhile the thing everyone actually needed from me just… doesn’t get done.
Did you have this same kind of trouble focusing when you were a child?
I’m not really sure. I don’t remember it being talked about that way when I was a kid. School was… school. I don’t know if it was the same thing.
Have you ever had a period when you felt unusually energetic and needed much less sleep than usual?

Yes. Most nights I only sleep maybe two or three hours. Sometimes I just end up on the couch with my laptop still open. But I don’t wake up tired, usually—I feel sharp, like sleeping was just… getting in the way.
When you’re sleeping only two or three hours and still feel sharp, is your mood unusually high or upbeat?

Yes… upbeat, I guess. More like everything is finally moving at the right speed. The lab feels almost electrified.

But if someone questions what I’m doing or tells me to slow down, I can get… sharp. I’ve snapped at people. Some of the students don’t really come by my office much now.
Do these times when you sleep only two or three hours and still feel sharp come in distinct periods, rather than being your usual pattern?
I guess it’s been more of a stretch than separate little episodes. About seven months now… since I took over the multi-site spectroscopy project.
During these past seven months, have you found yourself talking much more than usual or feeling like you can’t stop talking?
I don’t know. I mean… I talk when I need to explain the work. Maybe more than some people want. But I wouldn’t say I can’t stop.
During these past several months, have you felt more confident or important than usual?

Maybe. I mean… I did feel like I could fix the whole project myself. Redesign the spectroscopy approach, get the students on track better than their advisors were, and still make the grant deadline.

It didn’t feel like confidence exactly. It just felt… obvious that I could do it if people stopped getting in the way.
During this stretch, have you been taking on far more projects or work than usual?

Yes. I mean… probably more than usual.

I’ve been getting to the lab before everyone else, changing protocols, moving instrument time around, emailing collaborators overseas… starting analyses before the last ones are really finished. It just feels like if I sit still, I’m wasting the chance to get it all fixed.
Has this period caused serious problems at work or in your relationships?

Yes. At work, definitely.

My department has had to… step in on some decisions I used to handle myself. Scheduling got confused, priorities were missed, and I guess my supervision was getting strained enough that people were worried about the project and lab safety expectations. I don’t like saying that, but yes, it caused serious problems.
During these past seven months, have there been times when your thoughts were racing?
I’m not sure. I’ve had a lot on my mind, but I don’t know if I’d call it racing exactly. It’s more like… jumping between things, maybe. hard to say.
During this stretch, have you felt driven to keep starting or pushing ahead with work more than usual?

Yes… I think so.

I’ve been getting in before anyone else, changing protocols, moving instrument time around, emailing collaborators in different countries… starting new analyses before the other ones are done. It’s like if I stop, I’m wasting the chance to fix everything.
During this stretch, have you had experiences that others said were not true or not real?
No… I don’t think so. Not like seeing or hearing things, or anything like that. At least, nobody’s told me something was completely unreal.
During this period, did your symptoms ever lead to you being hospitalized?
I… don’t really want to get into all of that. I’m not sure how to answer.
During this period, did you ever believe something that other people said was not true?

I… yes, maybe. People pushed back on it.

I really thought I could fix the whole project myself—redesign the spectroscopy plan, straighten out the students’ work, still make the grant deadline. It felt obvious to me at the time that everyone else was just slowing things down.
During this period, were you ever admitted to a hospital because of these symptoms?
I’m… not sure I want to talk about that. It’s a little hard to say plainly.
Were you hospitalized for your mood or behavior during this period?
I don’t… I don’t really have a clear answer for that. I’d rather not go into it right now.
During this period, did your symptoms become severe enough that you could not do your job normally?

Yes. I mean… work didn’t just keep going normally.

My department had to step in on decisions I usually handled. I was missing priorities, getting the schedule confused, and… my supervision of people got strained enough that they were worried about the project, and lab safety expectations too.
Were you hospitalized because of these symptoms?
I… I don’t really want to answer that directly. I’m sorry. It’s just not something I can get into right now.
During this period, did other people tell you that your behavior was abnormal or that you needed treatment?
I’m not sure how to answer that. People were… concerned, I guess. I don’t remember anyone putting it to me exactly that way.
During that period, were you ever hospitalized because of your mood or behavior?
I… I don’t know that I want to go into that. I’m sorry. I’d rather not answer that directly.
